p: Human Horizon (“we”, “us”, “our”) is an AI consultancy and training firm based in Singapore. We help businesses build AI workflows into their teams’ work, train staff hands-on, and help the change stick.

This notice explains how we collect, use, disclose and look after personal data under the Personal Data Protection Act 2012 of Singapore (PDPA). It applies to personal data we handle through our website at humanhorizon.io, by email, in our business outreach and in the course of our engagements.
Our website is an information site with a contact form. It has no accounts or online payments. If this changes, we will update this notice before the change takes effect.
When you email us, we collect what you choose to send, usually your name, email address, job title, organisation and the content of your message.

When you use the contact form on our website, we collect your name, work email, company, team size, role, department and your message. Our website host, Netlify, stores the submission and sends it to us by email so we can reply. We use it only to respond to your enquiry.

When we explore or deliver an engagement, we collect business contact details of the people we work with. These include names, roles, work email addresses and phone numbers. We also collect information shared in meetings, workshops and training sessions, such as attendance, feedback and notes on how teams work.

When we reach out to businesses, we may collect business contact information that is publicly available. Sources include company websites, business directories and professional networks such as LinkedIn. We only collect information relevant to a business conversation.

When you visit our website, our hosting provider may process technical information such as your IP address, browser type and the pages requested. It does this to deliver the site and keep it secure. We do not use this information to identify you.

Our website stores one item in your browser’s session storage. It remembers whether you closed the announcement bar, so the bar stays closed while you browse. It contains no personal data and is cleared when you close the browser tab. We do not use cookies.
If we add other website features that collect personal data, we will update this notice to describe what is collected and why, and to explain any choices you have.
We use personal data for the following purposes:
To reply to your enquiries and keep in touch about matters you raised with us.
To prepare proposals, plan and deliver consultancy and training engagements, and follow up afterwards.
To manage our relationship with clients and their staff, including scheduling, invoicing and record keeping.
To contact businesses we believe may benefit from our services, using business contact information.
To send updates about our services where you have agreed to receive them or where the law otherwise permits.
To operate, maintain and secure our website.
To comply with legal and regulatory obligations, and to establish, exercise or defend legal claims.
We will not use your personal data for a new purpose without telling you and, where the PDPA requires it, getting your consent.

We collect, use and disclose personal data with your consent, or where the PDPA or other law allows us to do so without consent. You give consent when you provide your personal data to us for a purpose you know about, for example by emailing us with a question.

You may withdraw your consent at any time by emailing our data protection officer at the address at the end of this notice. We will tell you what withdrawing is likely to mean for you. For example, we may not be able to continue an engagement or reply to an enquiry. We will then stop collecting, using and disclosing your personal data for the purposes concerned, unless the law requires or permits us to continue.
Withdrawing consent does not affect our right to keep personal data where the law requires or allows it.
We do not sell personal data. We only disclose it where it is needed for the purposes in this notice, to the following:
Service providers who support our business, such as email, file storage, video conferencing and website hosting providers. They may only use the data to provide their services to us.
Professional advisers, such as lawyers, accountants and auditors, under a duty of confidentiality.
Government agencies, regulators, courts or law enforcement, where the law requires it or permits us to disclose without consent.
Any other party with your consent, for example a training partner you have agreed to involve.
Some of our service providers, such as our email and cloud storage providers, may store or process personal data on servers outside Singapore.

When we transfer personal data outside Singapore, we take reasonable steps to make sure the recipient protects it to a standard comparable to the PDPA. We do this as the PDPA requires, for example by relying on the provider’s contractual commitments.

We make reasonable security arrangements to protect personal data in our possession or control against unauthorised access, collection, use, disclosure, copying, modification, disposal and similar risks. These include access controls on our accounts, multi-factor authentication where available, and limiting access to those who need it.

No method of transmission over the internet or of electronic storage is completely secure, so we cannot guarantee absolute security. Please do not email us sensitive personal data that we have not asked for.
We keep personal data only for as long as it is needed for the purposes it was collected for, or for legal, accounting or business reasons.
When we no longer need it, we delete it, destroy it, or anonymise it so that it no longer identifies you.
We make a reasonable effort to make sure the personal data we use to make decisions about you, or disclose to others, is accurate and complete.
Please let us know if your details change or if you believe anything we hold about you is wrong.
You may ask us for a copy of the personal data about you that we hold or control. You may also ask how we have used or disclosed it in the past year.
You may ask us to correct an error or omission in your personal data.

To make a request, email our data protection officer. We may need to confirm your identity first. We will respond as soon as reasonably possible and within the time the PDPA allows. If we need more time, or cannot meet your request, we will tell you why, unless the PDPA allows us not to.
We may charge a reasonable fee for an access request. If we do, we will tell you the amount before we process the request.

h: Marketing messages and Do Not Call
p: We contact businesses mainly by email and professional networks. Every marketing email we send will tell you how to opt out, and you can also ask us to stop at any time by replying or emailing us.

If we send marketing messages to a Singapore telephone number by call, text or messaging app, we will follow the Do Not Call provisions of the PDPA. We will check the Do Not Call Registry where required, unless you have given us clear consent to contact you on that number.
If we become aware of a data breach involving personal data we hold, we will take prompt steps to contain it and assess it.
Where the PDPA requires it, we will notify the Personal Data Protection Commission and the individuals affected.

During an engagement, we may handle personal data that belongs to our client, such as staff or customer information. That data is handled under the engagement agreement and the client’s instructions. Where we act on the client’s behalf, the client remains responsible for it under the PDPA.
We use only AI tools and platforms that the client has approved for the engagement. We do not use client data to train AI models without the client’s written agreement.
If you are a client’s employee or customer, you can send questions about your data to the client. You can also contact us and we will help where we can.
Our services are for businesses and professionals. We do not knowingly collect personal data from children.
Our website may link to other websites, such as LinkedIn. We are not responsible for their content or privacy practices, so please read their privacy notices.
We may update this notice from time to time, for example if we add new features to our website. The latest version will always be on this page, with the date it was last updated.
If you have questions about this notice or how we handle personal data, or want to make a request, please contact our data protection officer at contact.humanhorizon@gmail.com.
If you are not satisfied with our response, you may contact the Personal Data Protection Commission of Singapore.
